messages:
mari: Quick heads-up — we’re seeing a big discrepancy in prefix cache behavior across deployments in EU. Hosted hit-rate ~78% vs Private (VPC) ~42% for the same workloads. p99 token latency also spikes in Private.

jake: Hmm, did you run the same traffic mix and warmup sequences?

mari: Yes — replayed 24h production trace against canaries. Same prompt set, same model commit. Snapshot: 
- Hosted (shared-netstore): hit-rate 78%, p50=12ms, p95=36ms, p99=48ms
- Dedicated (reserved GPUs + netstore): hit-rate 65%, p50=18ms, p95=80ms, p99=120ms
- Private (customer VPC + S3 over peering): hit-rate 42%, p50=40ms, p95=210ms, p99=320ms

sasha: That p99 for Private is concerning. Any netstore errors in logs?

mari: Yes — lots of GET timeouts and retry cascades. Sample: 
```
netstore GET key=sha256:abcd.. status=timeout duration=250ms
kv-cache fetch miss -> perform remote GET -> deadline exceeded
```

alex: Do keys differ? Could be keying mismatch between runtime variants (we added normalization in hosted earlier).

mari: Good call. I diffed the key generation code paths. Hosted runtime has prompt.strip().lower() normalization at the RPC ingester. Private nodes sometimes get prompts with trailing control chars from customer proxies, so keys don't match. Example differences: 
```
hosted key base: "user42|what's the weather" -> sha256(user42|what's the weather)
private incoming: "user42|what's the weather\n" -> different sha -> miss
```

natalie: So two issues: (1) key normalization drift, (2) VPC/netstore latency causing fallback to remote fetch + timeouts -> less effective warmup and smaller batch formation.

jake: On batching heuristics — we profile batching decisions and kernel selection. When cache hit-rate drops, more requests become cold and get sent as smaller batches, which triggers different kernels (no fused attention path) and lower throughput. That could explain higher p50 too.

mari: Exactly. I ran a microprofile: cold requests in Private show 1.8x higher per-token compute (different kernel) + netstore addtl 2-3x delay. Combined -> tail latency blowup.

alex: Any quick mitigation? We could: 
- apply normalization patch in runtime to unify keying (strip/normalize whitespace, collapse unicode NFKC)
- increase netstore read timeout + exponential backoff for VPC to avoid cascading retries
- add proactive warmup prefetch for common prefixes on Private (configurable per-deployment)

sasha: Also consider moving frequently-hit prefix shard to local SSD for Dedicated and Private where allowed. For Private on-prem customers we can provide an optional local cache service.

mari: I pushed a branch with normalization and a lightweight prefetch heuristic (prefetch top-2 prefixes per user during session start). Patch: 
```
// key normalize
string norm = normalize_nfkc(prompt).trim();
norm = collapse_spaces(norm);
key = sha256(user_id + '|' + norm);
```

natalie: Can we A/B canary the normalization only on Private first? Might avoid surprising hosted behavior.

deploy-bot: rolled canary 1805001320 -> runtime/cache-normalize:v2 on private-canary pool

jake: I instrumented an additional metric: cache_key_entropy and cache_hit_after_normalize. After canary rollout we saw immediate improvement: private-canary hit-rate -> 61% (was 42%). p99 reduced from 320ms -> 140ms.

mari: Nice. That confirms key-drift was a big factor. Remaining gap likely network/storage.

alex: For long-term: we should spec a deployment matrix in docs: required netstore latency SLOs, recommended local shard options, and default warmup thresholds per mode (hosted/dedicated/private). I'll draft and link.

natalie: Action items: 
- mari: open PR to backport normalization to all runtimes (PR #  / assign jake for review)
- alex: doc draft for netstore SLOs + local cache patterns
- sasha: evaluate SSD shard option costs for Dedicated and Private customers (cost/latency tradeoff)
- infra: test increasing netstore read timeout for VPC peering (needs safety limits)

mari: I'll also add an offline eval harness to replay customer traces with different warmup policies so we can tune prefetch thresholds without hitting prod.

jake: One more note — kernel selection fastpath sometimes uses sequence-length histogram to pick fused kernels. If our prefetch changes sequence length distribution, make sure to re-run kernel selector autosolver. We don't want to accidentally revert to slower kernels.

mari: Agreed — include that in the eval.

sasha: Thanks all. If nobody objects I'll expand the canary to 20% of private fleets after tests pass. :thumbsup:

alex: +1 from me. Keep the thread updated with PR links and dashboard links.

mari: Linking perf dashboards and PRs in follow-up comment once CI finishes. Thanks!
